title: Course Schedule II
summary: Return an order that completes every course once.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–2000 courses labeled from zero. Up to numCourses × (numCourses − 1) distinct pairs of different valid labels.
contractDetails.output-checking: Check the permutation and every prerequisite. Accept an empty array only when a directed cycle prevents completion.

statement: Return an order that completes every course once. A pair [course, prerequisite] means the prerequisite must come earlier. Return an empty array if no order can satisfy every pair. Any valid order is accepted.

examples.explanation: Course 2 can move anywhere as long as 0 comes before 1 and 1 before 3.
Every permutation is valid with no prerequisites.

constraints: 1–2000 courses labeled from zero. Up to numCourses × (numCourses − 1) distinct pairs of different valid labels.
hints: Conceptual: Only courses whose prerequisites have finished are available.
Directional: Maintain a queue of courses with no unmet prerequisites.
Implementation: Append each removed course, decrement its dependents, and return an empty array if the result is incomplete.
complexityAnalysis: O(V + E) time and space for Kahn’s algorithm.
